problem.name: Learning DNF from quantum examples
problem.statement_latex:
\textbf{Learning DNF under the uniform distribution.} An unknown $s$-term DNF $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ supplies uniform quantum examples. Output a classical hypothesis $h$ with $\Pr[h(x)\ne f(x)]\le\varepsilon$ and confidence $1-\delta$. Complexity counts examples and computation.

\textbf{Learning DNF under product distributions.} Given quantum examples of an unknown $s$-term DNF under a product distribution with $\mu_i=\mathbb E[x_i]\in[-1+c,1-c]$ for constant $c>0$, output a hypothesis of error at most $\varepsilon$. The marginal biases are known or learned as in the algorithm.

quantum.headline_latex: \textbf{Learning DNF under the uniform distribution.} $\operatorname{poly}(n,s,1/\varepsilon,\log(1/\delta))$ time and quantum examples by Bshouty--Jackson, combining Fourier sampling and boosting.
quantum.details_latex: \textbf{Learning DNF under product distributions.} $\operatorname{poly}(n,s,1/\varepsilon,\log(1/\delta))$ time for constant $c$, by Kanade--Rocchetto--Severini biased Fourier sampling and the product-distribution DNF learner.

quantum.details_text: Learning DNF under product distributions. $\operatorname{poly}(n,s,1/\varepsilon,\log(1/\delta))$ time for constant $c$, by Kanade–Rocchetto–Severini biased Fourier sampling and the product-distribution DNF learner.

classical.headline_latex: \textbf{Learning DNF under the uniform distribution.} $n^{O(\log(s/\varepsilon))}\operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta))$ time by classical low-degree approximation and uniform-distribution DNF learning. Classical membership-query learning is polynomial in the stronger active-query model.
classical.details_latex: \textbf{Learning DNF under product distributions.} $n^{O_c(\log(s/\varepsilon))}$ time by low-degree biased-Fourier approximation and classical regression; the general distribution-independent DNF learner has $2^{\widetilde O(n^{1/3})}$ time for polynomial-size DNF.
